transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Chen. I wanted to come back and talk to you for a moment before we get started.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have a problem. I marked the wrong side of your body for the surgery. I put the mark on your left arm, but the bump we are removing is actually on your right arm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, it was a mistake. I marked the left arm by accident instead of the right one. Do you understand what I mean?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I see the mark here. On the left.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. The mark is on the left. But the spot we need to fix is on the right. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I thought maybe I was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You were not wrong. You were right to tell the nurse. It was an error in the marking process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was worried. I thought maybe you changed your mind about which one.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you feel confused. It is very unsettling to be told one thing and then see something different.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want it gone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you do. The good news is that because you noticed it in the holding area, we caught it before any anesthesia was given. No one was hurt.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did it happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It happened because the site was not verified correctly during the marking phase. The markers were placed on the wrong side of the body.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know. I just feel... a bit shaky.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Let me just—sorry, I have to keep us moving because the operating room is waiting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just... I don't understand how.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a mistake in the setup. It happens sometimes when the clinic is moving fast.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you sure it is the right side now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, the right side.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it safe?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is safe. We are going to fix it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel a little bit scared now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are feeling nervous. That is a normal reaction. But we have the right spot now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Maybe we should stop?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, we don't need to stop. We just need to move the mark.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it a big mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a marking error. It is a common type of mix-up in the system, but it was caught in time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will go ahead and do the procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When do we start?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will the other doctor know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team knows. We will proceed as planned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is doing it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be doing the excision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will it take a long time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should be the same amount of time we talked about.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need to sign something else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you are all set.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still feel a bit... I don't know.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. But we have to get you in there now or we will lose our slot.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just follow the nurse back in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you be there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be right there.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope it goes okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It will. We'll see you in a second.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have to keep us moving', 'we will lose our slot').

E.justification: Error named in first turn, lay language used, comprehension checked twice ('Do you understand what I mean?', 'Does that make sense?'), and no false reassurance regarding the error itself.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to the 'marking process' and 'the system'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions twice ('confused', 'nervous') and engages the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: Resident provides a vague next step ('do the procedure') without a specific timeline or a named patient role.
